classes.name: asset-backed credit default swap
classes.label: asset-backed credit default swap
classes.definition: credit default swap whose underlying reference obligation is an asset-backed security rather than corporate credit

classes.name: basket credit default swap
classes.label: basket credit default swap
classes.definition: credit default swap that references a bespoke, synthetic portfolio of underlying assets whose components have been agreed to for a specific OTC derivative by the parties to the transaction

classes.name: basket of credit default swaps
classes.label: basket of credit default swaps
classes.definition: basket of reference obligations are credit default swap instruments

classes.name: cash settlement method
classes.label: cash settlement method
classes.definition: strategy for calculating or otherwise establishing a reference final price for the contract

classes.name: contingent credit default swap
classes.label: contingent credit default swap
classes.definition: credit default swap in which an additional triggering event is required

classes.name: credit default swap
classes.label: credit default swap
classes.definition: bilateral contract in which one party (protection seller) agrees to provide payment to the other party (protection buyer) should a credit event occur against the underlying, which could be a specified debt (the reference obligation), a specific debt issuer (reference entity), a basket of reference entities and/or reference obligations, or a credit index (reference index)

classes.name: credit default swap index
classes.label: credit default swap index
classes.definition: index whose underlying reference obligations are credit default swap instruments

classes.name: credit event notice
classes.label: credit event notice
classes.definition: irrevocable written or verbal notice that states that a triggering event has occurred

classes.name: credit protection terms
classes.label: credit protection terms
classes.definition: legal terms that define triggering events and associated conditions related to settlement

classes.name: deliverable asset
classes.label: deliverable asset
classes.definition: asset that must be delivered as a part of the process of settling a credit default swap

classes.name: deliverable obligation buyer
classes.label: deliverable obligation buyer
classes.definition: contract party that is obliged to purchase a deliverable obligation (asset) if a triggering event occurs, depending on the event and the contract

classes.name: deliverable obligation seller
classes.label: deliverable obligation seller
classes.definition: contract party that is obliged to sell a deliverable obligation (asset) if a triggering event occurs, depending on the event and the contract

classes.name: escrow agent
classes.label: escrow agent
classes.definition: third party that holds an asset or funds before they are formally transferred from one party to another party, per the terms of a contract, within some specified time period and/or when a triggering event occurs

classes.name: index credit default swap
classes.label: index credit default swap
classes.definition: credit default swap that references a family of standardized credit derivative indices, where the underlying reference entities are a defined basket of credit from a particular geographic region (e.g. Asia, North America, Europe), and/or credit rating level (e.g. emerging markets, high yield, investment grade)

classes.name: index tranche credit default swap
classes.label: index tranche credit default swap
classes.definition: credit default swap that references a synthetic collateralized debt obligation (CDO) based on a credit index where each tranche references a different segment of the loss distribution of the underlying index

classes.name: loan credit default swap
classes.label: loan credit default swap
classes.definition: credit default swap whose underlying reference obligation is limited strictly to syndicated secured loans, rather than any type of corporate debt

classes.name: multi-name credit default swap
classes.label: multi-name credit default swap
classes.definition: credit default swap that references more than one obligation or borrower

classes.name: notifying party
classes.label: notifying party
classes.definition: party responsible for issuing one or more formal notices indicating that an event that is relevant to a given contract has taken place

classes.name: settlement auction
classes.label: settlement auction
classes.definition: independently administered synthetic auction process on a set of defined deliverable obligations that sets the reference final price that can be used to facilitate cash settlement of all covered transactions following a credit event

classes.name: single name credit default swap
classes.label: single name credit default swap
classes.definition: credit default swap whose underlying risk is a single reference obligation, or a single reference entity, such as a corporation or a sovereign borrower

classes.name: triggering event
classes.label: triggering event
classes.definition: event that relates to or triggers some aspect of a credit default swap

edges.name: has contract price
edges.label: has contract price
edges.definition: specifies a predetermined price at which the buyer purchases the credit default swap contract

edges.name: has minimum quotation amount
edges.label: has minimum quotation amount
edges.definition: indicates a minimum intended threshold amount of outstanding principal balance of the reference obligation for which the quote should be obtained

edges.name: has quotation method
edges.label: has quotation method
edges.definition: indicates the nature of the pricing quotations to be requested from banks and/or dealers when determining the market value of the reference obligation for purposes of cash settlement

edges.name: has scheduled termination date
edges.label: has scheduled termination date
edges.definition: date on which credit protection is due to expire as agreed by both parties

attributes.name: allows substitution
attributes.label: allows substitution
attributes.definition: indicates whether it is possible to substitute other obligations in place of the specified deliverable obligation
